clips.environment: Pre-dawn interior of a Macedonian command tent at the Gaugamela camp: lamplight and a brazier, canvas walls, a simple cot. Two armed Macedonian guards stand motionless over the sleeping man. FIRST FRAME already shows this strange image.
clips.scene: LINEAR OPEN, hook front-loaded. Hazel whispers to her own lens while armed guards watch a sleeping man by lamplight; she glances back at the cot mid-line; the last ~3 seconds HOLD on her slow deadpan into the lens, no words.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (whisper): "Gaugamela. 331 BC. Tonight, an empire two hundred and twenty years old gets a new owner — and the man who's about to take it—" (glance back at the cot) "—is still asleep." Alexander sleeps; he never speaks.
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, arm's length, slight natural sway; the cot with the sleeping king readable behind her over her shoulder. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER asleep per his lock; Hazel scribe wardrobe established here and locked for the episode; guards' Macedonian gear only.
clips.sound: Tent-canvas rustle, distant camp murmur, brazier tick, her whisper.
clips.endingState: Her held deadpan filling frame, eyes to lens; cot and guards unchanged behind her.

clips.environment: Same command tent, minutes later; lamplight, first grey pre-dawn light at the tent flap.
clips.stillComposition: The instant Parmenion bursts in and shakes the waking king awake — Parmenion's hand gripping Alexander's shoulder, mid-shout, weight forward and tense. Alexander is caught mid-rise from the cot, one hand reaching toward his sword belt, face calm despite being startled awake. Hazel stands a few steps back and to the side, near the tent's edge, watching the exchange with alert attention — a genuine bystander physically present in the room, not narrating to any lens, hands empty at her sides. All three figures fully visible together in one wide external frame: Parmenion and Alexander form the foreground focal action; Hazel is a clear, readable secondary figure in the same space; believable eyelines and blocking; real depth and separation between the three bodies and the tent behind them. CAMERA: a real external observer's framing, eye-level, positioned inside the tent at a natural viewing distance, capturing all three figures together in one frame — no camera, phone, or rig in anyone's hand, no POV distortion, no fisheye, no arm's-length selfie perspective.
clips.scene: Parmenion strides in visibly rattled and shakes the sleeping king awake. Alexander wakes instantly calm, already reaching for his sword belt, unhurried. Mid-scene a wax tablet is pressed into Hazel's hands without explanation; she fumbles the stylus (running-gag plant).
clips.timeline: 0-1s: Parmenion enters, shakes him. 1-6.5s: Parmenion's two urgent lines land back-to-back (22 words @ 240 wpm). 6.5-8s: Alexander wakes calm, reaches for sword belt. 8-14.8s: Alexander answers, then asks Hazel (19 words @ 168 wpm, near-natural pace with emphasis, no multi-second silences). 14.8-15.2s: her hesitation beat, tablet freshly in hand. 15.2-17s: Hazel's answer (6 words @ 198 wpm).
clips.dialogue: PACING IS EXPLICIT PER CHARACTER AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY (corrected per short-form retention rule — near-natural rates, NOT sub-natural, weight carried by emphasis and pause PLACEMENT, never by an overall slow rate) — do not apply one uniform tempo across this exchange; the contrast between Parmenion's urgency (~240 wpm) and Alexander's measured calm (~168 wpm) IS the scene's performance point, sustained the whole clip. PARMENION (fast, clipped, breathless with urgency, shaking him, ~240 wpm): "My lord. MY LORD." — the second "MY LORD" louder and sharper than the first, no space between his two lines. PARMENION (still fast, words tumbling just behind his own movement, worked up, ~240 wpm): "You could have taken them in the dark last night. Why do you STILL refuse a night attack?" ALEXANDER (measured and economical at a near-natural pace, ~168 wpm — even while his hands move quickly buckling armor, his voice stays unhurried through EMPHASIS on key words and brief natural pauses between sentences, NOT multi-second silences and NOT a suppressed word rate): "I will not steal a victory, Parmenion. Let it be daylight, and let it be earned." ALEXANDER (to Hazel, still measured, ~168 wpm, half-amused, not rushed, looking directly at her as he speaks): "You write quickly?" HAZEL (HER EYES ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT DETAIL OF THIS BEAT: the instant Alexander's voice turns to address her, her eyes lift OFF THE TABLET and lock onto his face — this eye contact is held, unbroken, for the rest of the shot; she does NOT look back down at the tablet, the stylus, her hands, or anywhere else while she is speaking — a full beat of hesitation before she speaks at all — thrown by the tablet suddenly in her hands, not composed yet; then a dry, slightly startled-amused delivery, ~198 wpm (Hazel-only +10% stack applied), not swept into the room's urgency, fumbling the stylus by feel without looking at it, her gaze staying on Alexander's face the entire time she talks): "...Apparently—" (small pause) "—as of right now, yes." Only after her line fully ends and a beat passes does she finally look back down at the tablet.
clips.camera: A real external observer's frame inside the tent, all three visible together; the camera holds a natural viewing distance and reframes only to keep the group readable as they move — Parmenion looming over the cot, Alexander rising into it, the tablet pressed into Hazel's hands. EYELINES ARE THE MOST CRITICAL BLOCKING DETAIL IN THIS SHOT AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY: when Alexander speaks directly to Hazel ("You write quickly?"), his eyes are on her face, not on the middle distance or on Parmenion. Hazel's eyes are on the tablet ONLY during the brief silent writing beat before Alexander speaks to her — the MOMENT his voice turns toward her, her eyes come UP and lock onto his face, and stay locked on his face through her entire spoken answer; she is never looking down at the tablet, at her hands, off to the side, or at nothing while she is speaking or while he is speaking to her. This is a face-to-face exchange between two people who are looking at each other, not a woman absorbed in writing while a man talks near her. No POV, no selfie framing, nobody's eyeline is the lens. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: Both NPC locks verbatim; the wax diptych tablet and stylus debut here and are tracked for the rest of the episode. Alexander's unhurried pacing here is the same locked trait as every other clip (§32) — this scene does not suspend it, it is the scene that proves it.
clips.sound: Parmenion's footsteps and breath urgent, close, and quick; Alexander's own movements steadier and unhurried under his armor's small-sounds even as his hands work fast; canvas.
clips.endingState: Tablet in her hands, stylus recovered awkwardly; Alexander mid-arming; Parmenion still tense.

clips.scene: Arming continues through the WHOLE beat — he buckles, checks the blade, moves; the scene must never read as two people pausing to chat. She nods at the scroll-case; his answers land mid-motion; he is OUT of the tent on his last word — the scene exits into momentum.
clips.timeline: 0-0.9s: she nods at the scroll-case, asks (Hazel, 3 words @ 198 wpm). 0.9-6.7s: he answers without looking up, still arming (Alexander, 15 words @ 156 wpm, near-natural pace with emphasis, not a slow read). 6.7-8.8s: her line (Hazel, 7 words @ 198 wpm). 8.8-16.1s: his final line landing mid-stride (Alexander, 19 words @ 156 wpm, voice stays measured and economical through the exit motion, with one deliberate beat of contrast right before the final word). 16.1-18s: buckle snaps, glance lands, he exits frame.
clips.dialogue: PACING PER CHARACTER (corrected per short-form retention rule, plus the owner's +20% override on top of the researched bands): Hazel's is easy, curious, unhurried — a genuine question, not rushed, ~198 wpm. Alexander's VOICE conveys unhurried/economical through EMPHASIS and PAUSE PLACEMENT, not through an overall slow rate — his actual word rate is ~156 wpm; the 'unhurried' quality comes from a single deliberate beat of contrast right before his last word, not from a uniformly slow read, even as his HANDS and BODY move fast arming; his vocal pace and his physical pace are deliberately independent of each other, but his voice must never drag or sound sedated. HAZEL (easy, curious, mild wonder, unhurried, ~198 wpm; her eyes on him, watching him arm himself): "What's that?" ALEXANDER (his eyes are LOCKED ONTO THE LEATHER STRAP THREADING THROUGH THE BUCKLE in his own hands — a specific, continuous physical task his gaze tracks the entire line, the same way anyone watches their own hands thread a buckle; his eyes have a physical job to do and that job is not Hazel or the lens; voice measured and economical at ~156 wpm, weight carried by emphasis on "Aristotle's," "corrected," and "dagger," not by slowness): "Homer. Aristotle's own copy — he corrected it himself. Sleeps under my pillow. With the dagger." HAZEL (dry, a small amused edge at the image of a scholar-warrior sleeping with a book and a knife, still unhurried, ~198 wpm; eyes still on him): "You brought a book to a war." ALEXANDER (snapping the last buckle, already moving past her; his voice STAYS measured and economical at ~156 wpm even though his body is now in full motion toward the exit — one deliberate beat of contrast right before the final word "too," not a slow read throughout; his eyes track the buckle and then the sword hilt he checks with his hand as he strides — another continuous physical task, same as the first line — for the whole line UP TO the final word "too"; on "too" specifically, and ONLY on that word, his eyes lift FROM the hilt and land on her for LESS THAN ONE SECOND — a brief flick, not a held gaze — as he passes, then he is gone from frame): "I brought the only book that matters. Achilles didn't get old either. I intend to beat that record too."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens tracking his motion past her; she turns to follow his exit. EYELINES (anchored to physical tasks, not a bare instruction): Alexander's gaze is doing a specific job the whole clip — tracking the strap threading through the buckle on his first line, then the sword hilt his hand checks on his second line — never Hazel, never the lens, because his eyes are occupied with that physical task, not because he's told not to look. The ONE exception: his eyes lift off the hilt and land on her for LESS THAN ONE SECOND, starting only on the word "too" itself, not before it — a brief flick, not a held gaze, then he is already gone from frame; his eyes do NOT hold on her face for multiple seconds or through the words leading up to "too." Hazel's eyes are on him for the entire beat, unbroken — watching him arm himself, then turning to track his exit as he passes her; she never looks away from him. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER lock; motion never stops; scroll-case worn leather.
clips.sound: Armor small-sounds, canvas, distant horses waking.
clips.endingState: Tent flap swinging from his exit; she is turning to follow.

CRITICAL RULE: each army is ONE unbroken continuous mass along its own depth — there is NO empty ground inside either army's own footprint between its nearest and farthest visible ranks. The only permitted break in either formation is the single specific torn-gap feature described below — never a second large empty area. High aerial angle, close to straight-down; army coverage fills nearly the entire frame, with only ONE narrow strip of true open ground in the whole image — the no-man's-land directly between the two facing fronts. MACEDONIAN SIDE (nearer band): one continuous deep mass with no internal breaks — Craterus's pike phalanx in the center, sarissa points dense and unbroken; Alexander's Companion cavalry and hypaspists massed at the near-right edge of that same continuous body, already peeling off at a diagonal into the forming wedge; Parmenion's Thessalian cavalry massed at the left edge of the same body, held slightly back. All of it reads as one large touching army, not separate clusters. PERSIAN SIDE (rest of frame, to the horizon): one continuous deep mass, dramatically WIDER than the Macedonian side and extending well past both Macedonian flanks — light two-horse scythed chariots screening its leading edge merge directly into the massed ranks immediately behind them, touching, NOT a separate cluster with empty ground before the next; Darius and his elite guard (Immortals, Greek mercenaries) hold the center within this same continuous body; distinct cavalry wings are visible under different banners within it — Bessus's Bactrian/Scythian/Dahae cavalry nearer Alexander's advance, shown in motion, shifting to chase him; Mazaeus's Median/Parthian/Armenian cavalry on the far wing, banners and dress visibly different. The ONE permitted break: a gap — thinner, paler ranks, still part of the same continuous body, not a separate empty field — visible in the Persian center-left where Bessus's troops are shifting to chase Alexander's wing. Historical scale for density: Macedonian force ~47,000 in one compact, deep, unbroken formation; Persian force by the most-cited modern scholarly estimates (not the inflated ancient figures) roughly 90,000–100,000, several times wider and equally unbroken in depth.

clips.continuity: The chariot recedes deeper-right/away (geometrically honest — never toward a face-on camera); her battle-state heavy now: dust-caked, hair loose, tablet clamped.
clips.sound: The roar fracturing: individual cries closer, running feet, equipment clattering underfoot; her breath ragged and close.
clips.endingState: The collapse streaming past her; the chariot a receding speck; her eyes back to the lens.

clips.environment: Dusk at the camp's edge; the field's day visible on every person and surface; smoke columns far off; the camp erupting around his return — held LOW and distant. Wounded visible among the celebrating (the cost stays inside the triumph).
clips.scene: He returns dust-caked, Bucephalus lathered; he dismounts near her before anyone else reaches him, glances at the tablet still gripped tight in her now-steady hand; the exchange; he is already walking on, pulled into the noise.
clips.timeline: 0-3s: he rides in, dismounts near her; the camp's eruption stays low and distant. 3-6s: his glance at the tablet, his line — almost a smile. 6-8s: her answer, holding it up, no longer fumbling; he is already walking on.
clips.dialogue: PACING (owner +20% override applied to Alexander; +20% plus Hazel-only +10% stack applied to Hazel): ALEXANDER (almost a smile, warm, ~180 wpm): "Get all of it down?" HAZEL (holding up the tablet, no longer fumbling, confident, ~211 wpm): "Every word. Even the ones about stealing victories."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens; he enters the deep frame, dismounts into mid-frame near her; she turns between him and her lens. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER + BUCEPHALUS locks (horse lathered, led off behind him); her battle-state persists (dust, loose hair) but her hand is now steady — the running-gag payoff.
clips.sound: Camp eruption held LOW and distant (restraint); his voice and hers close; fires catching.
clips.endingState: He walks on into the noise; she watches him go, tablet lowered; cut lands on her exhale.

clips.environment: Dusk deepening, campfires relighting across the camp — a frame consciously rhyming clip 1's lamplit opening.
clips.scene: Outro part 1, talk-to-lens: the empire line lands as a weighty, matter-of-fact reveal — the gravity of the fact does the work, not a slowed performance. Ends on a held beat that sets up the hard cut into 9b's tonal pivot.
clips.timeline: 0-1s: beat, she settles to speak. 1-13.6s: the empire line (36 words @ 172 wpm — weighty but not yet softened). 13.6-15s: hold on her steady expression, hard cut to 9b.
clips.dialogue: PACING (owner +20% override plus Hazel-only +10% stack applied): weighty, matter-of-fact reveal — not rushed, not urgent; the fact's own gravity carries the pace via emphasis and phrasing, not raw slowness, target ~172 wpm. HAZEL (steady, direct to lens, matter-of-fact, not yet soft): "Cyrus built that empire two hundred and twenty years ago. It ended today, because a man who overslept his own war refused to win it in the dark — and because one king turned his chariot around."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, steady; campfires relighting in the deep frame behind her. EYELINE: her eyes stay on the lens/viewer for the entire line — she is not writing here, the tablet is held low and calm, out of her sightline, and her gaze never drops to it. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: Frame-rhyme with clip 1 (small warm lights in darkness behind her); tablet visible, held calmly, out of her eyeline; battle-dust softened but present.
clips.sound: Fires catching, low camp murmur settling, night insects beginning; her voice level and matter-of-fact — the softening begins in 9b, not here.
clips.endingState: Hold one beat on her steady expression after the line lands; hard cut to 9b.

clips.environment: Same dusk moment, continuing directly from 9a with no time skip — campfires relighting across the camp, frame still rhyming clip 1's lamplit opening.
clips.scene: Outro part 2, talk-to-lens: the softer Homer/Achilles payoff, then quieter still for the sign-off. This is the final shot of the episode — built around the one idea the viewer should leave with.
clips.timeline: 0-10.1s: (softer than 9a) the Homer/Achilles lines (29 words @ 172 wpm). 10.1-10.9s: beat, quieter still. 10.9-13.3s: (quiet) the sign-off (4 words @ 99 wpm, breath-constrained true-quiet delivery). 13.3-14s: hold, sign-off lands.
clips.dialogue: PACING PER BEAT (owner +20% override plus Hazel-only +10% stack applied): first beat noticeably softer than 9a's matter-of-fact delivery, carried by tone and phrasing not raw slowness — target ~172 wpm. Second beat quieter still — target ~99 wpm, genuinely quiet/breath-constrained, not just a text label. HAZEL (softer than 9a, still direct to lens, the affection under the fact now audible, brisk-but-soft): "He keeps Homer under his pillow. He wants to outlive Achilles. Twelve years from today, he's dead at thirty-two — and somehow that's still longer than he thought he'd get." (beat, quieter still) HAZEL (quiet, letting it land): "Hazel — out of time."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, steady, picking up immediately from 9a's hard cut — same continuous moment. EYELINE: her eyes stay on the lens/viewer through both lines, unbroken, including the sign-off; the tablet remains visible but out of her sightline throughout. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: Continues directly from 9a (same dusk light, same fire position, no reset); frame-rhyme with clip 1 (small warm lights in darkness behind her); tablet visible, held calmly, out of her eyeline; battle-dust softened but present.
clips.sound: Fires catching, low camp murmur settling, night insects beginning; her voice drops close and quiet across both lines, quietest on the sign-off.
clips.endingState: Her face lit by fire in the near-dark, the sign-off landing; hold one beat.
